title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: handle waiting conversations when a queue closes or has no representatives signed in
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the routing behaviour, opt-in setup and publishing-time credit consumption. Minor corrections should identify the API request properties, finish the editor guidance and align the risk rating with the opt-in default.

claims.claim: Queue is out of operating hours covers a queue closing while conversations are already waiting.
claims.quote: Queue is out of operating hours ... Evaluates whether the queue is outside its configured operating hours, including when the queue transitions out of operating hours while conversations are waiting.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: All representatives are signed out covers that state arising while conversations are already waiting.
claims.quote: All representatives are signed out ... Evaluates whether all representatives in the queue are signed out, including when this state occurs while conversations are already waiting.

claims.claim: The playbook's out-of-operating-hours condition is evaluated continuously, including after transfers.
claims.quote: The playbook condition is evaluated continuously, including after transfers.

claims.claim: The queue's own out-of-operating-hours overflow rule is evaluated once before queue entry, not when it closes with conversations waiting.
claims.quote: Use the queue is out of operating hours condition in the existing overflow rules on the Queue page and playbooks. The system evaluates the queue overflow rules once only before the system adds the work item to the queue.

claims.claim: Representative-availability overflow triggers immediately rather than waiting for time or volume conditions.
claims.quote: Configure overflow handling to trigger immediately when eligible service representatives aren't available for a work item or queues are out of operating hours, instead of waiting for time or volume-based conditions.

claims.claim: The cited documentation does not establish that writing the CC User Prompt record publishes a playbook or generates its runtime format.
claims.quote: Searched: msdyn_ccuserprompt Web API publish playbook structured runtime conversation orchestration. Read configure-conversation-orchestration and searched msdyn_ccuserprompt reference for publish/runtime; stage labels exist but no write-to-publish or conversion procedure is stated.

claims.claim: The medium risk rationale rates a published playbook rather than the opt-in control left at its default.
claims.quote: defaultState: admin-opt-in. Rationale: Medium. A published playbook can transfer, end or redirect live customer conversations on its own. Standard: low includes 'nothing happens until an admin opts in'; a new control is rated at its default.
claims.fix: Set risk to 'low' and replace the risk rationale with 'Low. No new fallback action runs until an administrator configures and publishes a playbook.' Retain the supported warnings about actions after publication.
